scope: Independent direct review of candidate01 exact source/diff and four focused regression cases; no tests, compilation, tracked edits or live actions

findings.problem: The observation only carries workers_settled (is_finished), remaining handles and the first error. Every case begins with an expected acknowledgement error. A later join Err is hidden by get_or_insert, yet is_finished=true and the consumed handle is None, so every current test can pass with a panicked created worker. Forced Node cleanup or phase-deadline failure can likewise remain hidden behind the first expected error while reaping/finished flags become true. This cannot satisfy the design requirement that additional forced/unconfirmed/resource failures remain failing evidence.
findings.source_counterexample: Keep the original startup-workers-incomplete or stdout-closed error, allow a created worker to panic and finish (join Err), or let Node be killed then reaped; the current expected result and all tested resource booleans/handle assertions still match. No fake outcome or runtime experiment was used to derive this source path.
findings.requested_fix: Expose narrow actual worker join outcomes and forced/cleanup-deadline facts in the existing private one-shot observation, and assert all expected created workers joined successfully with no additional forced/deadline cleanup failure. Preserve original typed constructor/close errors and existing clocks; no general observer framework or duplicated cleanup engine is needed.

findings.problem: The cached-failure Drop assertion accepts any panic, so an unrelated Drop panic would satisfy the claimed deliberate cached-error failure floor.
findings.requested_fix: Match the expected fixed original cleanup error in the caught panic payload, using a boolean/fixed-message assertion that does not print raw unexpected panic content. Keep the existing no-extra-cleanup observation checks.

checks.evidence: new() delegates to private new_observed(None,None). Each failpoint occurs only after actual Command::spawn, existing Self ownership and pipe extraction; no child/browser/provider replacement is introduced.
catch_unwind rejects constructor panic, matches exact startup error, requires post-cleanup observation before return, expected created handle set, and channel disconnection after Drop.

checks.property: Actual Node reap and created handle drain
checks.evidence: node_reaped is set only after actual Child try_wait status. Created handle masks are captured before actual cleanup; remaining handle masks after cleanup reflect consumed joins. Termination/reaping is observed, but successful joins and additional forced/deadline failures are not independently asserted (F1).

checks.property: Cached Err and no repeated attempt
checks.evidence: First real stdout-receiver failure is required; repeated close matches its result and emits no new observation. Drop must also emit no new attempt. Its any-panic assertion does not prove exact retained reason (F2).

One optional private unbounded mpsc sender emits after actual cleanup and result caching. Normal caller remains no-fault/no-observer; no public/environment/protocol or product surface is added. Keep this scope narrow.

Manifest and comments distinguish injected setup failure from empirical OS exhaustion. Browser custody is explicitly UNKNOWN; Node reaping does not establish browser group absence or temporary-file destruction. New emitted lines contain fixed metadata only, with no raw payload, node PID or exception output.

runtime_required_after_source_fix: Execute the four focused cases against unchanged actual Node fixture and updated source-pinned lifecycle probe.
Record expected/discovered/executed test counts and preserve any additional resource-cleanup failure.
Run unchanged short-family consumer and fresh full native/browser acceptance; focused or source acceptance alone cannot approve the product.
limits: The findings concern regression evidence strength, not a new implementation bug in the already-reviewed baseline cleanup owner.
No compilation, tests, fixture invocation, PID inspection or service actions were performed.
No browser absence or source/runtime GREEN is inferred.
